title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a very faint typescript carbon. It is clearly the same text as the cleaner next page, so the image should be read with that page. The heading is most likely "Catégories de Deuring", not "Tannaka". The section title is "Catégories A-linéaires et o-enveloppes" (possibly ⊗-enveloppes).

Setting.
- A is a commutative ring. C is an A-linear category: Hom's are A-modules and composition is bilinear.
- Let X be an object of C on which an A-algebra o acts A-linearly. Let P be a right o-module.
- The 'external tensor product' P⊗_o X is the object, if it exists, representing Y ↦ Hom_o(P, Hom_C(X,Y)). For P projective of finite type, this is the same as Hom_o(P^∨, X) (the margin note).

Admissible functors.
- An A-linear functor F: C → C' is called 'admissible' (compatible with external tensor product) if, whenever P⊗_o X exists in C, P⊗_o F(X) exists in C'. In addition, the canonical map P⊗_o F(X) → F(P⊗_o X) must be an isomorphism.
- The left margin records the dual notion, 'coadmissible': compatibility with internal Hom's Hom_o(P,X).

Reduction for Deuring categories.
- If C is a 'Deuring category', the condition need only be checked for one fixed object X, with o = End_C(X).
- One also need only take P in P(o/A), the right o-modules that are locally free of rank 1 over Spec A.
- The handwritten margin says it is enough that C has a 'strict generator' X. This means every object is P⊗_o X with P projective of finite type.

Morita / Eilenberg–Watts statement.
- In this situation, F ↦ F(X) is an equivalence.
- It goes from Hom_{A-adm}(C,C') to the category of objects X' of C' with an A-linear o-action such that P⊗_o X' exists for all such P.
- In any case, the category of admissible functors is A-linear.

The envelope.
- Put C(1) = Hom_A(C^op, Mod(A)), the A-linear presheaves.
- The Yoneda embedding i: C → C(1), X ↦ Hom_C(–,X), is fully faithful.
- C(1) serves as an envelope in which all external tensor products exist.

Purpose. This is foundational material for the 1965 'Galois theory of motives'. Motive categories are A-linear and generated by a single object, as with correspondences and Deuring-style endomorphism algebras of abelian varieties. Grothendieck wants to describe functors out of them, and their completions, through modules over End(X). In modern terms: tensored (copowered) enriched categories, Morita theory, and the Cauchy/Karoubi completion of a linear category.
errors: The OCR heading 'Catégories de Tannaka' is very likely 'Catégories de Deuring', judging from the image and the next page.
The rank condition is 'localement libres de rang 1', not rank n.
The Yoneda functor is Y ↦ Hom(Y,X), contravariant in Y. The OCR's Hom(X,Y) with C(X) is wrong; it should be C(1) = Hom_A(C^op, Mod(A)).
The next page has a typo: 'les Hom dans A' should read 'dans C'.

Gap: restricting the test modules to invertible (rank-1 locally free) P is only justified under the Deuring hypothesis. For a general strict generator one needs all finitely generated projective P, as the margin indicates. The page does not make this precise.

ideas.what: External tensor product P⊗_o X of a module over End-algebra with an object of a linear category, defined by representability
ideas.modern_name: tensored/copowered enriched category; action of Mod(o) on objects with o-action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (enriched categories, 1960s-80s); used in Deligne 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990) and Saavedra (1972)

ideas.what: Admissible functors = functors preserving these tensors; the dual 'coadmissible' = preserving Hom_o(P,X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: enriched category theory (Kelly); Street/Lawvere on absolute colimits

ideas.what: For C with a strict generator X, admissible functors C → C' are equivalent to objects of C' with an o = End(X)-action
ideas.modern_name: Morita / Eilenberg–Watts theorem for linear categories

ideas.what: Fully faithful Yoneda embedding into A-linear presheaves C(1) as an envelope
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exposé I (presheaf categories and Yoneda), in a non-linear setting

ideas.what: 'Deuring category': A-linear category whose objects are rank-1 twists P⊗_o X of a single generator
ideas.modern_name: no standard name; close to categories of motives or isogeny categories generated by one object

missed.claim: Grothendieck coins the term 'Catégories de Deuring' for A-linear categories generated by one object up to twisting by invertible End(X)-modules. He sets up a Morita-type description of their functors as a step in the Galois theory of motives. The terminology and this intermediate framework do not seem to appear in the literature.
missed.quote: Si C est une catégorie de Deuring, alors il suffit de poser cette condition pour un objet fixé X de C, et pour o = End_C(X), P un module ∈ P(o/A)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that in 1965 Grothendieck was formalizing motives via tensored linear categories and module twists over endomorphism algebras. This predates Saavedra and Deligne's treatment of external tensor products.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a standard Morita/enriched-category set-up, now routine. The only notable item is the unpublished notion and name 'Deuring category' in the motivic context.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Catégories de Deuring.' rather than 'Catégories de Tannaka.'
Section title: 'Catégories A-linéaires et o-enveloppes' (o possibly read as ⊗).
The algebra is denoted o (not α), and the module is P (not M).
'P un module ∈ P(o/A) = catégorie des o-modules à droite qui sont localement sur S=Spec(A) libres de rang 1', not rank n.
The functor reads 'F ↦ F(X): Hom_{A-adm}(C,C') → Mod(o,C')'.
'C(1) = Hom_A(C^o, Mod(A))' and 'C →i C(1)', with Y ↦ Hom_C(Y,X).
Left margin: 'notion duale "coadmissible": compatible avec Hom'.
